steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Doctor, we need to leave immediately.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I've found Kristen's energy source.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Things aren't yet irredeemable. The worst-case possibility I anticipate has not yet come to pass...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: We still have a chance to stop her.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Kristen's plan requires mass amounts of energy, the scale and purity of which are both beyond any modern Terran's grasp, or even their imagination.

options: So, she's exploiting the Sarcophagus's tech?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The sheer vastness of this energy is more than a Sarcophagus can provide, too.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I said, more than 'a' Sarcophagus.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I hadn't anticipated... their being in Columbia.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Buried right beneath these wastes.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Doctor, I need your help.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: And your help... is all I have.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Combat has concluded. She won't be in danger.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I ask you have faith in her. She may still be a child, but she is nevertheless a Rhodes Island Elite Operator.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: And I ask you have faith... in the time you've spent with her.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Whether the operation in Chernobog, or her days aboard Rhodes Island, not one past moment has been for naught, and these experiences likewise mold her even now.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: She will make her own choice, and we can only respect that choice.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: But... right now, as it falls to her, so it falls to us too.
7:45 P.M., H.A.M.H.R.R. now at upper S.H.A.F.T.
Incredible.
I've always wondered how you learned to fight so well, busy with all those research projects.
And I thought I made efficient use of my time. Do you never sleep?

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: What are you doing here?

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Ferdinand.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: You took the words right out of my mouth, Saria. After forcibly entering a Trimountian military spec ops bureau, what could you possibly be doing?

spans.text: You took the words right out of my mouth, Saria. After forcibly entering a Trimountian military spec ops bureau, what could

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: Let me guess. You want to find something to chase after that airborne gizmo.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: Maybe hijack a heavy duty army drone and tie yourself onto it, for example?

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: Or is that thinking a little too simple, Director Saria? I never took you for the impulsive type.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Out of the way, Ferdinand. I have no time to argue with you right now.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: Would you look at that, how sad. The only three... well, fine, Scientific Investigation's doesn't count. The only two Directors Control left out of her incredible master plan just happen to have gathered here.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: What do you want to do? Stop the madwoman?

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: Or... save her?

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: I have no need to tell you anything.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: I assure you, I don't mean to criticize your relationship with Kristen.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: I was just waiting for you.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: Listen, Saria. I'm not here to get in your way.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: I said, out of the way.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: And I said, 'listen.'

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: ...That's the sound of an aircraft.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Ferdinand, where is that one from?

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: The 'Horizon Arc Project' isn't just that superweapon Kristen's floating through the air. It's a complete strategic program.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: I tapped into some connections to borrow an aircraft they use to service 'Arc-01,' and blew up the rest while I was at it.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: Let me be clear. Look across all of Columbia, and you'll find very few passenger aircraft safely able to fly near barrier altitude.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: They won't need much time to scramble high-altitude craft from the District, but for you, and for me, that time is more than enough.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: You're proposing a collaboration.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: You believe—that you're seriously qualified for this?

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: There's the same old Saria I know.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: As though you'd have the ability to quell every single problem, even if I wasn't there to help.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: But I don't have a single shred of doubt about this.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: In your own words, there is no reason we should clash.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: H.A.M.H.R.R. has reached the S.H.A.F.T.'s aerial space, and the S.H.A.F.T. has begun accumulating energy.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: If we let this situation unfold as is, then no matter what Kristen's up to, this will end with the Department of Defense exposed to the winds of scrutiny.

spans.text: If we let this situation unfold as is, then no matter what Kristen's up to, this
end with the Department of Defense exposed to the winds of scrutiny.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: And I'm sure we all know how Rhine Lab, as an 'accessory' to it, will end up.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: And whether it be as a clandestine military proxy, or a former Director of Rhine Lab, you'll be finished, Ferdinand.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: Exactly.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: But I'm not about to give in.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: We can still make it in time.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: We can bring H.A.M.H.R.R. back down again in a safe descent before the energy excitation, and then there will be room to pull everything back.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: And is it your life you're looking to redeem, or Rhine Lab?

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: Does it matter?

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: You'll have to be franker than that, Ferdinand.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: You've been ready with this aircraft. You've been anticipating that Kristen could get this far.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: Here I'd thought the busywork at Defense had ground away all your researcher's insight.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: Still, I've been ready for less time than you think.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Do you honestly believe this adventure of yours will rescue anything?

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: If you didn't think so, then why would you be here?

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: Do you know what feeling has struck me deeper than anything else lately?

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: I feel like nobody cares about Rhine Lab's reputation.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: Everyone else is either out to see what research funds Rhine can get them, or their only interest is in what Kristen's doing.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: You may have considered how Kristen leaves the picture, but have you considered what will become of the company afterwards?

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: Yes, I know, you've all been captured by her charm and charisma.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: With a little soul-searching, I have to wonder if I wasn't too? Of course I was.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: But Rhine Lab is ours, of the blood we shed. I can't accept her setting fire to everything that I gave the sweat of my brow for.

spans.text: But Rhine Lab is ours, of the blood
shed. I can't accept her setting fire to everything that I gave the sweat of my brow for.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: No matter what reason drives it.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: So I can swallow being a tuskbeast of the military, because I want to pull Rhine back from the brink. Is that so wrong?

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: I never thought I'd see you telling me this sort of thing.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: They're very Director of Defense-like words, aren't they?

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: Frankly, I should be getting a cut of your salary for it.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: I am no longer the Director of Defense.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: Fine. Once the dust settles on all this, I'll talk with Jara about getting a raise.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: You'll need to be reemployed first.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: Still, you were right about one thing.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: Rescuing Rhine... is far from my only aim.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: I need Rhine, and Rhine needs me. That's my assessment, borne of reason and emotion.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: However—

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: To put it bluntly, I'm curious.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: This is Kristen we're talking about. We know Kristen. The army wants to think she's out to blow something up, which is stupid.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: After working with her for so long, we know what kind of woman she is, and of course, you would understand her better than I ever could.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: Saria, tell me straight. What's going on in that brain of hers?

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: How far is she going to take this?

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: I can conjecture.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: Conjecture. Very cautious terminology.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: Go on, then. Are you conjecturing or not?

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Those drones currently on the attack may be unable to pierce H.A.M.H.R.R.'s armor for the time being, and cannot reach its altitude of hover.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: But shooting down this maintenance aircraft of yours would be simple enough for them.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: My guess is, the military and Maylander are deploying even greater firepower right now. Specialist drones capable of even higher altitudes. Even landing craft to convey troops. Their involvement in the front line is only a matter of time.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: We need to get your little craft, with near to no armor and not a single weapon installed, straight through a net of drone fire.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: This definitely carries a little risk.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: I'll pilot.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: Suit yourself.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: Are you actually able to run this thing, though?

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: ...I learned, once. In college.
7:50 P.M., H.A.M.H.R.R. altitude 3000 meters

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Ungh...

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: It seems like... the Transmitter response... has started growing stronger.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: It should be... right around here.

steps.name: Researcher
steps.text: Still no good!

steps.name: Researcher
steps.text: Energy readout's completely blanked!

steps.name: Columbian Soldier
steps.text: You can't stop it?

steps.name: Researcher
steps.text: Not that! The thing's blown past max display capacity!

steps.name: Researcher
steps.text: There's nothing in the manuals for this!

steps.name: Columbian Soldier
steps.text: Then to hell with the manual! I want solutions, dammit!

steps.name: Researcher
steps.text: No, no, no, the entire facility's energy supply lines should be cut by now, all of them...

steps.name: Researcher
steps.text: This energy... where the heck it coming from?

steps.name: Columbian Soldier
steps.text: So you're telling me, this energy is enough to turn us to ash with just one lick, but it's just coming out of thin air?

steps.name: Researcher
steps.text: Uh, the burden is on you to prove that hypothesis...

steps.name: Columbian Soldier
steps.text: Shut up, and keep giving me solutions, or I'll hurl you straight in there!

steps.name: Researcher
steps.text: Let me just give it another once-over, pipelines... switches... energy nodes...

steps.name: Columbian Soldier
steps.text: Is this... Is this son of a bitch gonna explode on us?

steps.name: Researcher
steps.text: The manual says... uh, I think, in general terms, current accumulated energy is now beyond the structure's theoretical safe capacity.

steps.name: Columbian Soldier
steps.text: If it explodes, what happens?

steps.name: Researcher
steps.text: I... I don't know...

steps.name: Columbian Soldier
steps.text: Hey... Okay. Run me some analysis.

steps.name: Columbian Soldier
steps.text: If something does go wrong... will it hit Yorktown? That's not far from here!

steps.name: Researcher
steps.text: Y—Yorktown? I'm not sure...

steps.name: Columbian Soldier
steps.text: Tell me how big it'll blow, for Pete's sake!

steps.name: Columbian Soldier
steps.text: I told my brother-in-law it was a bad idea to pioneer out near Trimounts! It's a city of headcases!

steps.name: Researcher
steps.text: I-I'm calculating now!

steps.name: Columbian Soldier
steps.text: To hell with this, I'm surrounded by science nuts! Crazy poindexters!

steps.name: Columbian Soldier
steps.text: Don't any of you have even a single breaker in your brains? Every day with your million fricking amazing projects and you never just, uh, WONDER what happens if you screw up?

spans.text: Don't any of you have even a
breaker in your brains? Every day with your million fricking amazing projects and you never just, uh, WONDER what happens if you screw up?

steps.name: Columbian Soldier
steps.text: The minds behind Trimountian science! And you build this giant bomb that activates itself and you literally can't even shut it down?!

steps.name: Researcher
steps.text: I wasn't on this project! I got temp assigned to work on this by your colonel!

steps.name: Researcher
steps.text: I—I would've definitely tested this thing a few more times myself...

steps.name: Columbian Soldier
steps.text: Zip it! I know you people too well. One little teensy-weensy hint of success and it's like you all go goddamn blind!

steps.name: Researcher
steps.text: But... wasn't this project led by the DOD?

steps.name: Columbian Soldier
steps.text: Okay, then they're ALL insane! I warned my meemaw when she said her folks were coming to pioneer in Columbia! Nation built of goddamn nutcases!

steps.name: Columbian Soldier
steps.text: Dammit, are you done calculating?! Shit, this won't work, I need to make a call...

steps.name: Columbian Soldier
steps.text: Why can't I dial out?

steps.name: Researcher
steps.text: Energy concentrations are too high, probably, uh, thus impacting signal transmission...

steps.name: Columbian Soldier
steps.text: Dammit! God—DAMMIT!

steps.name: Columbian Soldier
steps.text: Is there anywhere with better signal? Some other corridor?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: This has all fallen into chaos.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Energy transmission... can't be halted? Just what is Kristen trying to do?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Mmm...

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Transmitter response is still growing stronger...

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: It should be that the Transmitter Professor Parvis tuned is all aboard H.A.M.H.R.R., so why is there such a strong reaction here too?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Ugh... I have to...

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Is there a passage anywhere? I need to keep heading down.

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: *sigh*. Silence.

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: So you came. You chose this path to move forward.

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: Whenever Parvis recruited for his places, he'd always tell me that the trait he most valued was a researcher's perseverance for 'progress.'

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: No wonder he graded you well.

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: What... What could be on your mind right now?

steps.name: Jara
steps.text: Kristen.

options: Kristen, she've kept her secrets so very well.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: For the past while, I investigated several former Trimounts locations surveyed by Rhine Lab, until finally I found this place.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: And the reality was little removed from what I imagined.
Kal'tsit gives the rock face beside her a few knocks.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: We're separated from the 'Horizon Arc Project' S.H.A.F.T. by only a few hundred meters. I'm afraid Kristen has the way laid out there too, should you want to go sightseeing.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: ...Dr. {@nickname}.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I presume you've gathered that there is much more driving Rhodes Island to intervene so actively in the Trimounts affair, beyond simply who and what you've seen.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Silence, Ifrit and Saria, Loken and Rosmontis—even the revenant calling himself the Tin Man. All of them are simply ordinary people, far separated from the truth.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: With regards to the Rhine Lab commotion and Kristen going out of control, the military and the Maylander Foundation are like weights once again placed on the scales, trying to preserve the semblance of a civilized nation.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: But none of that is what matters most, what should concern most.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: From the very beginning, Kristen has been brushing against something far beyond anyone's imaginations, and with that as a focus, has launched a charge against the sky.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I worry her actions will bring unexpected things to bear upon Terra. My intent was to stop her before then... but we were one step too slow.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: On Terra today, interfering in such things is no longer easy. Civilization is much more expansive than I thought.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: There'll come a day when people step far enough again.

options: Why not share what you know with anyone else?
Isn't Kristen just trying to break through the sky?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: It's not as if I haven't before, but the end result is never ideal.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: You may suggest those aboard Rhodes Island today, Amiya, Closure, the hunters with ties to Ægir... They know a great deal already, which has helped to resolve their own issues.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: But when you plough the fields, you never pay mind to why the horizons form as clouds, rain and lightning, yet perhaps you may want to know when the next storm will come.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The arrogant acts of noble politicians versus repeated Catastrophe, the forecasted yield of crops versus new tax levies, these are things that ground life. The reality is, countless have no regard for even that much.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: They simply do not care for the fates of others.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: From a Terran's point of view, even if they did choose to believe such far-flung knowledge and information, what could they do about it? What use would it be?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The wise that take note of all around them, those bare few, are the only ones able to maintain their thought.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: And the rest, when faced with things that outstrip their comprehension, more than often opt to laugh it off or persecute it, so as to protect their comfortable bubbles of ignorance from any outside challenge.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: They are no more than 'lamentable,' but the truth grows ever further because of them.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: 'Breakthrough.' A neutral descriptor, but you still unconsciously believe that the 'sky' is something that should have no limit.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: To any scholar across the land, all that happens high in the sky is unsolved natural phenomena, just as Catastrophe and the ocean are.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: They will puzzle, probe at its inner workings, use their knowledge and philosophies to dissect it all—they will research all the phenomena of the sky, never considering that 'the sky should not be this way.'

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Countless children have flown for it in their dreams, and they too quickly realize, the sky is not something that can be freely soared through.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Drones and vehicle altitudes have been rigorously restricted, and the spreading of every fowlbeast's wings is constrained by instinct.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: This is the state of common sense upon this land. No one has ever questioned the rising of the sun and setting of the moon, and no one has ever questioned how it is all that all beings come to grow.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: But Kristen has steadfastly chosen 'not to believe,' just as poets do not believe that dreams are fiction.

options: You've been pushed to explain to me before.
I'm starting to wonder just what's ahead of us.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Just promise me one thing, Doctor.

options: As if I have a choice?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: No matter what it is you find next, and think next, do not let it shake you. I am by your side.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: If you choose to... No. No, you won't.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I trust the you that accompanied Amiya and Rhodes Island to today, and I trust that you're prepared in your own way.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Despite how inescapably scarce our remaining time is.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: —Wait.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Fall back, Doctor. What I just said will take some explaining.
You follow Kal'tsit's gaze far, to where a dangerous silver glint perches atop the rock.
A woman clings to the stalactite wall with nothing but her tail, almost like she's floating in the air, taking in the two of you with great amusement.
You feel uneasy.
It isn't Ho'olheyak's sudden appearance before you, rather that you realize how Kal'tsit, of prudence comparable to an automated machine, has made a mistake so rudimentary, even to you.
Ho'olheyak gently lands beside the two of you. Her mirthful smile draws scratches across your beating heart.

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: I thought you were more cautious than that, Rhodes Island physician.

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: But to be fair, mm-hmm... I'm surprised you two managed to find this place. Kristen never even told me its exact location.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: K'uk'ulkan.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Betraying the Maylander Foundation is tantamount to funeralizing your future in Columbia. What Kristen promised must be far more generous than what Maylander could give you.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: You and your clan chose a path of no return. And you're trying to find the source of your race's power from Control and Loken's research.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I advise you to stop. This is not pursuit of the historical self, it is simply self-destruction. A vast time has elapsed in which the Elders have lost their legendary powers, and now compared to the remaining Ancient races, have no—
Kal'tsit's speech is interrupted.
Ho'olheyak's tail has quietly pressed against your throat.

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: Yes. There's a sort of pressure your calm expression and tone of voice wreak. One that makes your database of a brain capable of turning words into weapons.

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: But you know that sometimes... speechcraft just doesn't work.

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: The Sarcophagus from Loken and the files Kristen got from who-knows-where are enough to round off this dream we've had for a long time, a dream filled to bursting with power and might.

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: Look at this now... look at me. My plumage, my flesh, my tail. Memory tells me how it's all begotten by my blood, a high blood by any other name. The K'uk'ulkan blood.

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: I'm very strong, aren't I, 'Doctor?'

options: Please loosen your tail when you speak.

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: Hahah... I don't mind your composure one bit. But, you see, if I felt like snapping your neck, then it wouldn't take much effort to do it.

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: I remember it happening just like this before. Without all that fantastical equipment, Kristen's hardly stronger than the average person, and I could've just as easily throttled her.

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: But she downplayed, minimized. Rejected 'power.'

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: I don't really like the oddball scientist type, but she made me realize—outside of my lineage, what do I even have?

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: It's a cruel irony. The words she says cling to you. She humiliated the calling and the memories I succeeded. I wanted so badly to return the favor—

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: —but she seemed so impossible to strike at. The placidity, like she'd gotten everything life had to offer.

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: So placid, it made me... envious. Made me want to claw myself apart, it shook me so badly.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: She... won you over?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: What is it you want?

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: I want to see how she ends, to guess her true intentions, to unearth her legacy. And then, I'll snatch away every last little thing that made up her mind when she ridiculed me.

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: Maybe I'll find the answer, just like that. Before I return to my longed-for age of the K'uk'ulkan's unrivaled dominance, I want to know, in our modern sense, what worth that has—

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: —what worth I have.

steps.name: Ho'olheyak
steps.text: That's what I, Ho'olheyak, want to do. I hope you won't get in the way, 'Doctor,' Dame Kal'tsit.
